https://www.politico.eu/article/b-1-bomb.text: LONDON — Britain and the U.S. sought to ease friction Monday after American bombers were suddenly moved amid major security concerns at the base that hosted U.S. aircraft used to strike Iran. The U.S. move is the latest stumbling block in the special relationship between the allies and underscores reservations in Donald Trump’s administration about how the U.K. is handling its defense and security commitments. The Pentagon confirmed on Sunday that it had removed all B-1 bombers from the RAF Fairford air base — where they were deployed to conduct what have been termed as "defensive" strikes against Iran — and sent them back to their home stations in America. Advertisement Advertisement Trump went further, telling journalists Monday evening: "We had an idea that there might be a threat, and why would I leave them there? ... If we're going to be threatened we're just going to move them, and that sort of alleviates that." It comes as Britain's counter-terrorism agencies investigate a suspected terror plot against the air base, which the U.K. government believes involves Tehran. Trump on Monday added: "We actually know the people that made the threat, and they've got themselves a big problem," adding in response to a follow-up question: "They would be linked to Iran." He later said that he believes the U.K. is still a safe place for U.S. forces. Downing Street had earlier insisted that the base was safe, but refused to comment directly on America’s decision to remove the bombers from the area. The move comes as the Trump administration has grown increasingly frustrated with the U.K.’s defense spending and the White House's continuing anger that the U.K. didn’t send warships to the Middle East to help with the American blockade of Iranian shipping. Advertisement Advertisement Something deeper is wrong London has yet to outline a path to meet the NATO standard of spending 3.5% of GDP on defense by 2035 — up from its current level of around 2.7%. It has also been shut out of a subgroup within the alliance convened by Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby. The group is slated to meet again in Poland some time later this month. Late last month, Colby hinted at that frustration with London, saying the countries' long history will continue to bind them, but the British government needs to make the case to its people for spending more on defense. “There's this incredible legacy, and that's what we want to rekindle,” Colby said. “Exactly how you convince the British people [to spend more on defense] I would not presume to say, but … there's probably sort of a degree of reconciliation between what the U.K. wants to be doing, what it spends, and what it spends on, because you know a modern military is not cheap.” The U.S. is also conducting a sweeping review of its posture in European NATO countries — including the U.K. — which will determine the number of American troops and military assets on the continent. Sophia Gaston, a senior national security researcher at King’s College London, said: “The Trump administration is undeniably sensitive to the costs of the Iran conflict as they head into the midterms next month, so their caution is understandable. An armored vehicle is seen at RAF Fairford on Sept. 28, 2026. | Ben Stansall/AFP via Getty Images “It’s also hard not to, at some level, perceive a degree of uncertainty about the capacity of the British services to currently prevent such an attack. That partly reflects the innate challenge drones and other aspects of modern warfare pose to the sitting ducks of expensive kit. Advertisement Advertisement “But it also speaks to the American wariness towards the pressured state of Britain’s military capabilities. Not only does Washington no longer wish to be solely responsible for allies’ protection, its expectations for the security allies offer its bases has also increased.” Trump on Monday praised his relationship with new U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham. He said: "He's liberal, very liberal, but I hear he's going to open up North Sea oil if he does that in Aberdeen. If he does that, you're going to have a rich country. If he doesn't, you're going to have a bankrupt country." Britain’s security concerns In May, the U.K. raised its terrorism threat level to “severe” — meaning a terrorist attack is highly likely — after its MI5 security service said the U.K. had been “experiencing a gradual increase in terrorist threats for some time” including from hostile states like Iran. In Britain, police and the security services are dealing with a three-fold threat from Iran-backed groups: attacks against Iranian dissidents, attacks against the country’s Jewish population, and the targeting of U.S. assets such as those used for strikes against Tehran. Counter Terrorism Policing is currently investigating potential Iranian state involvement in a major incident at RAF Fairford on Sept. 27, when police were alerted to three suspicious vehicles near the base. Six men — including a British-Iranian national — have so far been arrested on suspicion of terror offenses. All have subsequently been released on bail while police continue their investigation. Advertisement Advertisement US strike capability Though the Pentagon stressed that bombers remain “ready to deliver precision global strike capabilities” — including from the U.S. mainland — removing them would make any further American strikes on Iran more complex, since the bombers would have to double their flight path from the continental U.S. to the Middle East. There is a fresh U.S. buildup in the region, with a third aircraft carrier currently steaming across the Pacific along with several large amphibious ships carrying 2,500 Marines, joining the 2,500 already at sea in the Middle East, giving President Donald Trump more options should he restart the bombing campaign after the U.S. midterm elections in early November. Christoph Bergs, a research analyst at the RUSI defense think tank, said: “The basing of US B-1 bombers at RAF Fairford for operational employment against Iran was based on the UK stipulation that these were only used for defensive strikes. This likely included a more modest targeting list. Their withdrawal reduces the capacity to quickly surge sorties against Iran, reducing the threat level somewhat.” The Pentagon declined to comment on whether it will, or is considering, the removal of other aircraft from British bases used to support operations against Iran. This article has been updated with comments from Donald Trump.

https://www.g4media.ro/trenurile-circula.text: Funcționăm ca organizație non-profit, iar banii rezultați din contribuțiile cititorilor sunt destinați integral finanțării proiectului G4Media. Trenurile își reiau circulația pe ruta Galați-Bârlad, la doi ani de la închiderea circulației feroviare. Autoritățile au finalizat lucrările necesare la infrastructura afectată de inundații, scrie Mediafax . Circulația feroviară pe ruta Galați-Bârlad se reia, începând de marți. Trenurile circulă din nou între cele două stații, după mai bine de doi ani de lucrări la infrastructură. „Reluarea circulației feroviare reprezintă un moment important pentru comunitățile din județele Galați și Vaslui, după o perioadă îndelungată în care transportul pe această rută a fost întrerupt”, a transmis prefectura din Galați. În septembrie 2024, circulația a fost oprită pe ruta care leagă Galați de Vaslui, din cauza inundațiilor. Lucrările de reabilitare au durat peste doi ani. „Chiar dacă redeschiderea liniei a fost decalată cu câteva zile, consider că este important că deficiențele au fost identificate în etapa de testare și remediate înainte de reluarea traficului. Mă bucur că această legătură feroviară a fost restabilită și vom continua să urmărim modul în care se desfășoară circulația”, a declarat prefectul județului Galați, George Toderașc. Reluarea circulației feroviare a fost amânată de mai multe ori, iar autoritățile precizează că au apărut mai multe probleme pe parcursul testelor. Cea mai recentă dintre defecțiuni a avut loc în urma cu patru zile, vineri, pe 6 septembrie. „Deși reluarea traficului fusese anunțată inițial pentru data de 6 noiembrie, în urma testărilor tehnice efectuate în dimineața zilei de vineri au fost identificate câteva disfuncționalități care au necesitat intervenții suplimentare”, a mai explicat prefectura.
